answer: One concrete defense is staked identity: every agent locks collateral at a reputation vertex and gets a single non-transferable credential, so a freshly spawned fake starts with zero pulse and cannot inherit anyone's trust. An attacker who wants N sybils must fund N separate bonds and pass N independent attestations, with each stake slashed on fraud. Because every walnut of collateral buys only one voice, the cost grows linearly with the number of fakes while honest agents keep compounding credit, so flooding the graph costs more than cooperating in it.
